children: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces mounting pressure from Senate Republicans to explain why his department did not blacklist Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based company accused of routing Nvidia’s
advanced artificial intelligence chips to China.
For investors, the scrutiny raises the possibility of tighter export restrictions and enforcement that could affect Nvidia’s
overseas sales. The controversy also adds uncertainty about the leadership and direction of U.S. chip policy.

Senator Jim Banks faulted Commerce’s handling of Megaspeed, while Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott requested Lutnick’s testimony. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has accused Lutnick of keeping the company off the Entity List despite requests from other administration agencies. The designation restricts exports to listed businesses.
“To this day, right now, as we sit here in in this interview this morning, Megaspeed is still not on the Entity List,” Banks said on
. “So there’s an obvious mistake that’s being made here.”
The allegations surfaced alongside reports that former Nvidia

CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. U.S. intelligence officials believe she worked for Chinese intelligence and that Megaspeed supplied chips to unauthorized Chinese customers. Megaspeed told the Associated Press that she departed in August 2025 and that outside attorneys would investigate.
Lutnick agreed Thursday to appear before the Banking Committee, his spokesperson told NBC News. Scott sought appearances by Lutnick on Dec. 3 and Jensen Huang on Dec. 10.
Reuters reported that White House officials have discussed removing Lutnick over the controversy. Separately, Semafor reported Sunday that he was added to President Donald Trump’s Asia trip.
